key_insight: In agentic reinforcement learning, a privileged self-teacher is not always helpful, and its value changes across training stages. RetireOPD proposes to use self-on-policy distillation only when it is actually beneficial, then retire it when it becomes unreliable or unnecessary.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the mismatch between sparse trajectory-level RL rewards and the need for dense token-level supervision in multi-turn agents, while also tackling the instability of self-teachers in agentic tasks.
method: Use self on-policy distillation (OPD) to convert a trajectory-level reward signal into dense token-level supervision for a student agent.
Rely on a self-teacher with privileged task skills, but monitor when its guidance is trustworthy and when it degrades learning.
Introduce a self-retiring strategy that disables teacher supervision at stages where it no longer helps, making distillation stage-aware.
impact: This work helps practitioners train more reliable multi-turn agents by avoiding overreliance on flawed teacher guidance. It suggests that distillation should be adaptive, not always-on, improving stability and efficiency in agentic RL.

paper_title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yan Yu, Zhengxi Lu, Yizhou Liu, Yichen Pan, Aozhe Wang
